source_text: Οὐδὲνοὕτω τῷ θεῷ μεγαλοπρεπές, ὡς λόγος κεκαθαρμένος καὶ ψυχὴ τελεία τοῖς τῆς ἀληθείας δόγμασιν. Μόνον ἀμετάπτωτον ἀγαθὸν καὶ παραμένον ἡ εὐσέβεια.
thought_title: Pure speech and a perfected soul as what is magnificent to God; piety as the only abiding good
orientation: The speaker continues the collection of maxims, now stating what is most magnificent to God and what alone is an unchangeable good.
pass_a_gloss: Nothing [is] so magnificent to God, as [a] word [that has been] purified and [a] soul [that has been] perfected by the teachings of the truth. Only [an] unchangeable good and [one that] remains [is] piety.

choices.why: The glossary bans 'purified word' but the drafter vote and the literal sense of λόγος as word/speech require a rendering; 'pure speech' is the glossary English, so I use 'purified word' in the literal gloss to preserve the participle's passive perfect force, while the natural gloss uses 'pure speech' per the glossary.
The glossary English is 'perfected soul'; the adjective τελεία here means brought to completion by the teachings of truth, not merely 'mature' or 'complete' in a neutral sense.

The glossary English is 'teachings of truth'; I keep the article 'the truth' because the source has τῆς ἀληθείας with the definite article, and the phrase refers to the specific body of true doctrine.

The two adjectives modify ἀγαθόν; 'unchangeable' renders ἀμετάπτωτον (not liable to fall or change), and 'abiding' renders παραμένον (remaining, enduring). The natural gloss joins them with 'and' before the noun for English idiom.
rejected: good that does not fall away and remains

choices.why: The glossary mandates 'piety' and bans 'devotion', 'godliness', and 'religion'.

pass_b_english: Nothing is so magnificent to God as pure speech and a soul perfected by the teachings of truth.
Piety alone is an unchangeable and abiding good.
